The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

persons.name: Edward Richards Allen
persons.note: THE LADDER'S OWN READING OF THIS EVIDENCE. Read from directory_1843, newspaper_letter_list, poll_1834. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1834 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). OLD SETTLERS, 1882 — CORROBORATION, NOT A NEW FACT ABOUT 1835. The Calumet Club's fourth annual reception to the settlers of Chicago prior to 1840, held 18 May 1882, printed this man among the guests present as “Allen, Edward R., Aurora, Ill.” (Chicago Tribune, 19 May 1882). The club's criterion was residence in Chicago before 1 January 1840 and majority by then: the roster therefore corroborates a pre-1840 Chicago residence and says he was alive in 1882. It gives NO year of arrival, and the address it prints is where he lived in 1882, forty-seven years after the scene date — it is not an 1835 residence and is not read as one. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Allen, Edward” (poll_1834_004, line 173). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Allen' agrees with the entry's forenames; 3 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

transcribes.work: Poll list for the first election of Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago (10 August 1833)
transcribes.note: 30 entries. Andreas says twenty-eight men voted at this election; the list prints thirty names. T-0542 searched for a count outside Andreas and found none — the Chicago Democrat did not exist until 26 November 1833 and its whole run to August 1835 carries no retrospective count of this poll — so the discrepancy STANDS, with the negative search recorded (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v004). On weight the thirty are the enrolments and Andreas's twenty-eight is an 1884 belief-statement ('It is believed') about the number of legal voters; neither count is repaired.

transcribes.work: Tax List of the Town of Chicago - 1833
transcribes.note: 115 entries. Names only — as published it carries no valuation, no lot and no figure, so it is not a ranked property roll (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v001).

transcribes.work: Election Returns - Poll List of 1834, filed 11 August 1834
transcribes.note: 115 entries. Andreas independently dates the second town election to 11 August 1834, which corroborates the list's own heading.

85 entries. THE LIST PRINTS NO DATE, AND IT IS NOT THE POLL BOOK OF THE THIRD TOWN ELECTION. That election is now dated from the town's own newspaper rather than from Andreas: the Chicago Democrat of 8 July 1835 announced the election of Trustees under the new charter for 'Friday of this week' and the issue of 15 July reported that it 'took place on Friday last' with the return — FRIDAY 10 JULY 1835, nine days after the 1835-07-01 scene date (claims/town_election_1835_democrat.json d001-d005). Andreas's town chapter, 'in July, 1835', is corroborated; his police chapter's 5 August 1835 is the day the newly elected board sat and passed the town's ordinance code over Hugunin's name as President. But that return gives single candidates 124 and 142 votes, which 85 men cannot cast, and six of the ten men who stood are absent from these 85 while the list runs unbroken from Adams to Wright — so this is a DIFFERENT poll, not a short printing of that one (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v003). Which poll is open; the county and state general election of Monday 3 August 1835 is the nearest candidate. Until it is settled, a name here evidences presence in Chicago in 1835 and not presence on any particular day.

what_it_supplies: 345 names of men who voted at, or were taxed by, the Town of Chicago in 1833, 1834 and 1835, as printed
which of the four lists each name stands on, and its position in that list
the courtesy and rank titles the lists print in front of a name (Col., Lt., Major, Dr.)

for the 1835 poll list: presence in Chicago during 1835, which is the strongest residence evidence this project holds short of a newspaper naming the man — but NOT presence on a stated day, because the list is undated and is shown not to be the poll book of the 10 July 1835 town election (T-0542)
what_it_does_not_supply: any address, street, lot or dwelling
any age, trade, household or family member
any date more precise than a list's own heading — and the 1835 list has no heading date at all
any woman, and any man who neither voted nor was taxed
